title: Binary output length and running time
statement: Let $F$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $R,T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every input word $y$, the machine halts within $T(|y|)$ steps with output the binary digit word of $R(|y|)$. Then, for every Boolean word $x$, the length of the binary digit word of $R(|x|)$ is at most $T(|x|)$.
hypotheses_covered: F is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
R and T are functions from natural numbers to natural numbers
F computes the binary digit word of R(|y|) on every input y within T(|y|) steps
replaced:
Let $F$ be a bundled finite machine over the Boolean alphabet that computes, in time
$T$, the function sending each input $x$ to the binary digit word of $R(|x|)$. Then for
every input $x$, the length of that digit word is at most $T(|x|)$, since a run can
append at most one output symbol per step.
